# Code Morph

A code panel morphs between versions of a file: surviving tokens glide to their new line and column, removed code blurs out and new code fades in. The clip is 4.6 s long for the default two versions and 36-frame morph.

Category: ui-blocks. Length: 4.6 s. WebGL: no.

Use when:
- A launch or product demo needs to show an API getting simpler, with before and after code in one panel and the surviving tokens visibly travelling to their new places.
- A refactor, a new SDK call or a config change should read as one continuous edit instead of a hard cut between two screenshots.
- A walkthrough builds one file up in two to four steps, each change landing on a highlighted line.

Avoid when:
- The code should simply appear line by line, with no before and after: use a code block reveal.
- The code should be typed out character by character: use a terminal or typewriter effect.
- The camera should scan a long file while it reveals.

Variables:
- filename (string): Filename, default "invoices.tsx"
- code_before (string): Code before, default ""
- code_after (string): Code after, default ""
- morph_at (number, 0-200): Morph at, default 48
- steps (string): Steps, default ""
- theme (enum): Theme, default "dark"
- accent_color (color): Accent, default "#0ea5e9"
- morph_duration (number, 12-90): Morph frames, default 36
- font_size (number, 12-32): Font size, default 20
- highlight (boolean): Highlight changes, default true
- line_numbers (boolean): Line numbers, default true
- window_dots (boolean): Window dots, default true
- speed (number, 0.25-4): Speed, default 1

Source: https://github.com/Remocn/remocn. Licence: MIT. The scene file keeps the upstream notice.
